title: In Short Supply: Efficiency Implications of Rational Attention Allocation
eligible_reason: Binary treatment (options listing on a firm's close industry peer; ddiff = peer x post) switching on at firm-specific years with 18 adoption cohorts (yeartp 1996-2013) and never-treated matched controls (firms whose options were already listed in 1996 and that are excluded from peer matching). Tables 2 (cols 1-3), 3 (cols 1-3), 4 (cols 1-3), 7 (cols 1-2) and Figure 2 are linear reghdfe regressions on an unstacked firm-year panel (the construction log forces one observation per firm-year, lines 17718-17743) with firm FE (gvkey_cohort) and calendar-year FE interacted with the unit's time-invariant adoption cohort (year_cohort), no controls, clustered by firm. By the letter of PROTOCOL Section 2 these are eligible static TWFE / unstacked event-study specifications on a matched sample. JUDGMENT CALL for the lead: the cohort-by-year FE make every identifying comparison within-cohort (peers vs their matched never-treated controls), which is closer in spirit to a stacked design without duplication; Callaway-Sant'Anna would have to be run with the matched never-treated controls to target the same estimand. Columns 4-6 of Tables 3-4, cols 3-4 of Table 7, and Figures 3-6 use the explicitly stacked file (gvkeyCohort, timeCohort) and are ineligible; Tables 5, 6, 8, 9, 10 add continuous interactions.
design_notes: Sample construction (replication_sampleconstruction.log): treated = firms with options listed after 1996 (yearlisted); already-listed-in-1996 firms (aol) are the control pool. Peers = one Mahalanobis match per treated firm at t=-1 on mcap, std, tvol within year x SIC (mahapick; duplicates on gvkey dropped so each peer has one cohort). Controls for peers = Mahalanobis match on ln_at and prof within year x 3-digit SIC x size quintile from the aol pool (1,656 controls, 1,710 peers; yeartp distribution 1996:621 ... 2013:86 rows). Panel: Compustat-CRSP 1993-2018 joined by gvkey to the peer/control list; after joinby, 'duplicates drop gvkey year, force' leaves one row per firm-year (18,643 duplicate rows deleted), so a control matched to several peers keeps a single cohort per year (cohort may differ across its years, splitting it into several gvkey_cohort units). time_all = year - yeartp; ddiff = 1 if peer==1 & time_all>=0; post = time_all>=0. FE: gvkey_cohort = group(gvkey yeartp); year_cohort = group(year yeartp). Table 1 N(anno) = 11,711. The 'listed_control_staggered' file applies the same structure to the newly listed firms themselves vs matched controls (Table 2, Figure 2). The 'stacked' files (Tables 3-7 right-hand columns, Figures 3-6) expand firms across cohorts and add not-yet-treated peers as controls with post-treatment rows dropped.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: yeartp (peer's listing year) takes 18 values, 1996-2013 (construction log tab, line ~17610); Figure 1 plots listings 1997-2014 after adding one year.
modern_estimator_note: Full-text hits for 'Callaway' and 'Goodman-Bacon' (candidates.csv flags) but no csdid/did_imputation/eventstudyinteract call appears in the replication log; the stacked regression is the remedy adopted.
preferred_spec_note: Abstract highlights declines in attention and price informativeness, higher volatility, and lower profitability for peer firms; Table 3 col 1 (analyst coverage) is the headline. Preference between staggered (cols 1-3) and stacked (cols 4-6) columns cannot be determined without the text.

data_files_note: Every .do, .dta and .tex entry in _archive_mnsc.2024.07233.zip has length 0 (only macOS resource forks accompany them), so the archive as uploaded contains no code, no data and no tables. Even a complete upload would ship synthetic data (README: 10% firm subsample, anonymized gvkeys, outcome and characteristic values shuffled across firms within year, treatment/event-time/FE identifiers preserved) that cannot reproduce the published estimates. Original data are WRDS Compustat-CRSP, IBES and options-listing records. All regression commands and published coefficients were recovered from the logs.
software_notes: Stata; reghdfe, estout/esttab, parmest, coefplot, insobs, mahapick, winsor2.
priority_note: Eligible by the letter of the rules (with the cohort-by-year FE judgment call) but no usable code or data in the package; replication requires the authors' original panel. Published coefficients and SEs for all eligible specs are recorded from the log.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text; data/packages/mnsc.2024.07233_regressions.txt is empty because the do-files are empty).
